prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your business size, industry, budget, channels you want to focus on (SEO, paid ads, content, social, email, growth/analytics), and your goals/KPIs. I can help you find the best match if you tell me more, but here’s a practical way to choose plus next steps I can do for you.

Questions I need to narrow options
- What are your primary goals? (e.g., revenue growth, lead gen, brand awareness, user acquisition)
- What channels matter most? (SEO, paid search, social ads, programmatic, email, content, influencer)
- Industry / target market (B2B, B2C, enterprise, SMB, vertical)
- Monthly/annual marketing budget (rough range)
- Timing / duration (short campaign vs long-term retainer)
- Must-haves (experience with SaaS, e‑commerce, multilingual campaigns, privacy/compliance, tech stack)

How to define “best”
- Track record with businesses like yours (case studies and outcome metrics)
- Measurable KPIs and reporting cadence
- Team expertise and senior involvement (not just offshore juniors)
- Tools and tech (analytics, attribution, ad platforms, martech)
- Transparency in pricing and deliverables
- Client retention and references you can call
- Cultural fit and communication style

Quick agency-vetting checklist (what to ask and check)
- Ask for 2–3 case studies showing specific metrics (CAC, ROI, MQLs, conversion lift)
- Request references from current or recent clients (similar size/industry)
- Who will be your day-to-day contact and what are their credentials?
- What tools/platforms do you use and what’s included vs extra cost?
- What exact deliverables/timeline for the first 90 days?
- Reporting frequency and KPIs tracked; do they provide raw data access?
- Pricing model: hourly, project, performance, retained? Cancellation terms?
- Red flags: vague results, no references, unwillingness to sign SLAs

Typical agency fits by need
- Growth / performance marketing for startups: look for agencies with user-acquisition and paid channels experience, A/B testing, and strong analytics.
- SEO / content-led growth: agencies with technical SEO and content strategy + editorial capabilities.
- Enterprise / complex B2B: firms with ABM, CRM integration, lead-scoring and multi-touch attribution experience.
- E‑commerce: agencies focused on paid social, shopping, CRO and email automation.

What I can do for you right now
- Create a short RFP template you can send to agencies
- Build a scoring matrix to evaluate proposals
- Draft an outreach email to 5–10 vetted San Francisco agencies (if you want me to find them, I’ll need permission to perform a web search or you can share a shortlist)
- Shortlist 5 agencies tailored to your answers above and include pros/cons

If you want specific agency names and a tailored shortlist, tell me your goals, budget, and channel priorities and I’ll prepare a recommended list and outreach materials. Which direction do you want to go?
